Documented debugging/triage under pressure: 'Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture)' on the COFFIN capstone maps directly onto the JD's 'triage product or system issues... debug/track/resolve' responsibility.

Performance optimization instincts are real and quantified (CUDA kernel work: 35% speedup via memory coalescing; TensorRT YOLO: 5.2x speedup) which is the kind of evidence a 'performance... debugging' preferred qual is actually checking for.
MS Computer Engineering from RIT satisfies the preferred degree qualification outright.
real_gaps: Zero full-time years against a stated '2 years experience' minimum. The bachelor's line explicitly allows 'or equivalent practical experience' but the two technical-experience lines don't carry that same qualifier.
RTOS depth is one hobby project (FreeRTOS on the Object Tracking Turret) — mutexes and task coordination, real but small in scope, not 2 years of production RTOS work.
DSA is coursework-only, not demonstrated anywhere (no LeetCode, no DSA-specific project) — matches the standing feedback-resume-defensibility note that DSA prep is an active, unresolved gap.
'Large scale systems data analysis' doesn't match your actual scale: CUDA/TensorRT/MPI-SLURM work is edge-device and academic-HPC scale, not production distributed systems.
Gerrit: zero exposure anywhere (Git/GitLab experience exists, Gerrit specifically does not).
'Visualization tools' evidence is thin — only a single-user PyQt/Matplotlib lab GUI at BARC, not large-scale systems observability tooling.

No code review experience anywhere in the profile, despite the JD explicitly naming 'review code developed by other engineers... style guidelines, checking code in, accuracy, testability, efficiency.'
No testing/testability evidence anywhere — no unit tests, CI, or QA process in any project; everything is single-developer work.
'Design reviews... deciding amongst available technologies' leadership evidence (Robotics Club GS, BraTS team lead) is academic/extracurricular, not a professional engineering-org context.
Documentation experience is thin and dated (2022-2023 internship bullets only, not engineering-org scale).

XR is the team's actual product and the job title itself; the only touchpoint is a 2022 internship bullet describing a Mixed Reality headset CONCEPT (documentation + BOM), not shipped XR software or device firmware. Single biggest domain gap; keyword match never scored it.

C++ depth is a repeat interview failure mode (NVIDIA: couldn't answer 'what did you use from C++17', failed 2 other C++ questions) — same risk surfaces again on a C++-heavy embedded role. See feedback-resume-defensibility.

STM32/FreeRTOS project framing has caused confusion before (COFFIN=Arduino vs Turret/drone=STM32/FreeRTOS) — current tailored resume keeps this straight, but be ready to defend which project used which MCU under direct questioning. See project-coffin-repo-landmines.
Sensor-tradeoff reasoning under live questioning is a named, learnable gap (TBC R3 GPS-denied sensor-selection question), not bad luck — worth drilling before any embedded/robotics-adjacent screen.
overstated_by_keywords: 'Embedded operating systems' was marked a clean Have — accurate for skill presence, but the underlying evidence is one university project, not 2 years of production RTOS work the JD line is nominally asking for.

'Performance / large-scale systems data analysis' was marked Adjacent-with-good-coverage by the keyword pass, but the actual gap in scale (embedded/edge and academic-HPC vs. production distributed systems) is larger than 'adjacent' suggests.
llm_analysis.reasoning: The core technical bar (low-level C on bare metal, real RTOS experience, debugging discipline) is genuinely met with concrete project evidence, not just keyword presence, which is stronger than a typical new-grad match. But the keyword-only 100% score hides two real risks: this posting sits on Google's XR team specifically and Justin has no hands-on XR work, and the '2 years experience' line has no full-time backing, resting entirely on internship-equivalence that isn't guaranteed to read favorably at screen.
